proposals.observation: 7 sessions landed on the quiz intro in 48 hours and zero started — a 0% start rate. Every visitor is stopping at intro_load without advancing a single step. This is the single largest conversion leak in the funnel right now.
proposals.proposal: Replace the current intro screen copy with a lower-friction, ICP-specific hook that names the tension directly — something grounded in 'the story beneath the money' rather than a generic invitation. Add a single, clear, unambiguous button label that tells the visitor exactly what the first step is. Remove any secondary links or navigation visible on the intro screen that offer an escape route.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality type and get a personalised breakdown of how it might be holding you back.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does money still feel like a problem?

This 3-minute quiz maps the quiet pattern underneath your spending, saving, and avoiding — and tells you exactly what it means.

No email required to start.
proposals.impact: Lift quiz start rate from 0% toward 20–40% of landing sessions

proposals.observation: The 'Fred Apply' GitHub Actions workflow failed 3 times in under 2 hours on 2026-04-29 (09:14, 09:14, 10:12), and 'Funnel-Hack Digest' also failed the same day. Four of 12 workflow runs in 24 hours are failing. This means Fred's own optimisation proposals are not being applied automatically, compounding every other issue silently.
proposals.proposal: Add a minimal error-notification step at the end of the Fred Apply workflow that posts the failure reason to a Slack webhook or writes a plain-text file to a known path (e.g. .fred/last-error.txt) so the failure mode is visible without opening GitHub. This is a single step addition to the workflow — blocked path is .github/workflows/* so instead, create a lightweight diagnostic script Fred can trigger manually: a shell script that dry-runs the apply logic and writes a human-readable diff to .fred/apply-debug.txt.
proposals.new_text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run from repo root to diagnose Fred Apply failures
# Usage: bash .fred/debug-apply.sh
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== Fred Apply Debug $(date -u) ==="
echo "Checking for proposals file..."
ls -lh .fred/proposals.json 2>/dev/null || echo "ERROR: .fred/proposals.json missing"
echo "Checking node version..."
node --version
echo "Dry-run applying proposals (no writes)..."
node .fred/apply.js --dry-run 2>&1 | tee .fred/apply-debug.txt
echo "Output written to .fred/apply-debug.txt"
proposals.impact: Surface the root cause of 3+ consecutive Fred Apply failures so they can be fixed in one targeted edit

proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 57% open rate versus 40% for Money Avoidance and 37.5% for Money Worship. The Vigilance sequence is resonating significantly more with its segment — likely because its subject line or framing speaks more directly to the careful-but-stuck pattern that matches the ICP (earns well, doesn't build). The other two sequences are underperforming and losing warm leads at email open before they ever reach a sales touchpoint.
proposals.proposal: Audit the subject line of email 1 in the Money Vigilance automation. Extract the structural pattern (e.g. named tension + specific cost + no resolution promised). Apply that same structural pattern to the subject lines of email 1 in Money Avoidance and Money Worship. This is a two-line subject-line edit per automation — one file if sequences are stored in a single content file, otherwise two separate files.
